## PR Description

## gh-1507: Boot-path main-isolate hang — boot watchdog + boot-step breadcrumbs

### Root Cause
TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch (iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) with no crash log. The freeze signature matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads) before `runApp`, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs more awaited main-isolate disk reads behind the boot spinner. With only a screenshot report and no sysdiagnose, the exact wedged step was unidentifiable — and the reporting build was 12 versions behind main because the TestFlight leg was failing (#1472, fixed in #1482).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` (new): `BootSteps` — a process-wide boot-step ledger (step name + uptime, in-flight step tracking); `BootWatchdog` — fires a diagnostic breadcrumb if the first frame does not land within the threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS=` override, `0` disables), then re-fires every 30 s until the first frame; a late first frame logs the recovery with uptime and firing count. Breadcrumbs ride the existing `debugPrint` tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb trail).
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/app_boot.dart`: watchdog installed right after the window stage in `run()`/`runWithEnv()`; step marks at every stage boundary and around every persisted store load in `loadBootStores`.
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart`: step marks around the post-frame restore (`restore:env` / `restore:manager` / `restore:session`) so a wedge after the first frame is equally diagnosable.
- Boot-path audit (AC2): pre-frame work is inherent to the staged await boot; network surfaces are already non-blocking or guarded (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, 180 s provider connect watchdog). No blind deferrals — moving store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.

### Test Coverage
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` (new, 9 tests): ledger ordering/in-flight/cap, threshold firing, 30 s repeat, first-frame cancel, late-frame recovery line, install idempotency — all PASS.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/` — 26/26 PASS.
- CI subset (323 files: non-golden, non-`cli_visual`, `--exclude-tags integration`): 3678 passed, 108 skipped, 2 failed — both in `providers_queue_writer_io_test.dart`, caused by `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` leaking into this runner's shell env (they pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, 10/10; CI does not set the var). Golden/`cli_visual` failures in an unfiltered local run are host-locked per the ci.yml golden comment.

### Notes
- Cannot repro on an iOS device from this environment; the build-gap statement (AC1) stands on the stale-TestFlight-build root (#1472/#1482). Next stale freeze will carry the exact boot step in Crashlytics breadcrumbs / debug logs.
- Behavior is additive-only; the watchdog never changes boot semantics.

## PR Description

Closes #1507
## gh-1507: Boot-path main-isolate hang — boot watchdog + boot-step breadcrumbs

### Root Cause
TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch (iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) with no crash log. The freeze signature matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads) before `runApp`, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs more awaited main-isolate disk reads behind the boot spinner. With only a screenshot report and no sysdiagnose, the exact wedged step was unidentifiable — and the reporting build was 12 versions behind main because the TestFlight leg was failing (#1472, fixed in #1482).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` (new): `BootSteps` — a process-wide boot-step ledger (step name + uptime, in-flight step tracking); `BootWatchdog` — fires a diagnostic breadcrumb if the first frame does not land within the threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS=` override, `0` disables), then re-fires every 30 s until the first frame; a late first frame logs the recovery with uptime and firing count. Breadcrumbs ride the existing `debugPrint` tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb trail).
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/app_boot.dart`: watchdog installed right after the window stage in `run()`/`runWithEnv()`; step marks at every stage boundary and around every persisted store load in `loadBootStores`.
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart`: step marks around the post-frame restore (`restore:env` / `restore:manager` / `restore:session`) so a wedge after the first frame is equally diagnosable.
- Boot-path audit (AC2): pre-frame work is inherent to the staged await boot; network surfaces are already non-blocking or guarded (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, 180 s provider connect watchdog). No blind deferrals — moving store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.

### Test Coverage
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` (new, 9 tests): ledger ordering/in-flight/cap, threshold firing, 30 s repeat, first-frame cancel, late-frame recovery line, install idempotency — all PASS.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/` — 26/26 PASS.
- CI subset (323 files: non-golden, non-`cli_visual`, `--exclude-tags integration`): 3678 passed, 108 skipped, 2 failed — both in `providers_queue_writer_io_test.dart`, caused by `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` leaking into this runner's shell env (they pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, 10/10; CI does not set the var). ## PR Description

## gh-1507: Boot-path main-isolate hang — boot watchdog + boot-step breadcrumbs

### Root Cause
TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch (iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) with no crash log. The freeze signature matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads) before `runApp`, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs more awaited main-isolate disk reads behind the boot spinner. With only a screenshot report and no sysdiagnose, the exact wedged step was unidentifiable — and the reporting build was 12 versions behind main because the TestFlight leg was failing (#1472, fixed in #1482).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` (new): `BootSteps` — a process-wide boot-step ledger (step name + uptime, in-flight step tracking); `BootWatchdog` — fires a diagnostic breadcrumb if the first frame does not land within the threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS=` override, `0` disables), then re-fires every 30 s until the first frame; a late first frame logs the recovery with uptime and firing count. Breadcrumbs ride the existing `debugPrint` tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb trail).
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/app_boot.dart`: watchdog installed right after the window stage in `run()`/`runWithEnv()`; step marks at every stage boundary and around every persisted store load in `loadBootStores`.
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart`: step marks around the post-frame restore (`restore:env` / `restore:manager` / `restore:session`) so a wedge after the first frame is equally diagnosable.
- Boot-path audit (AC2): pre-frame work is inherent to the staged await boot; network surfaces are already non-blocking or guarded (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, 180 s provider connect watchdog). No blind deferrals — moving store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.

### Test Coverage
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` (new, 9 tests): ledger ordering/in-flight/cap, threshold firing, 30 s repeat, first-frame cancel, late-frame recovery line, install idempotency — all PASS.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/` — 26/26 PASS.
- CI subset (323 files: non-golden, non-`cli_visual`, `--exclude-tags integration`): 3678 passed, 108 skipped, 2 failed — both in `providers_queue_writer_io_test.dart`, caused by `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` leaking into this runner's shell env (they pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, 10/10; CI does not set the var). Golden/`cli_visual` failures in an unfiltered local run are host-locked per the ci.yml golden comment.

### Notes
- Cannot repro on an iOS device from this environment; the build-gap statement (AC1) stands on the stale-TestFlight-build root (#1472/#1482). Next stale freeze will carry the exact boot step in Crashlytics breadcrumbs / debug logs.
- Behavior is additive-only; the watchdog never changes boot semantics.

## gh-1507: Boot-path main-isolate hang — boot watchdog + boot-step breadcrumbs

### Root Cause
TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch (iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) with no crash log. The freeze signature matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads) before `runApp`, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs more awaited main-isolate disk reads behind the boot spinner. With only a screenshot report and no sysdiagnose, the exact wedged step was unidentifiable — and the reporting build was 12 versions behind main because the TestFlight leg was failing (#1472, fixed in #1482).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` (new): `BootSteps` — a process-wide boot-step ledger (step name + uptime, in-flight step tracking); `BootWatchdog` — fires a diagnostic breadcrumb if the first frame does not land within the threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS=` override, `0` disables), then re-fires every 30 s until the first frame; a late first frame logs the recovery with uptime and firing count. Breadcrumbs ride the existing `debugPrint` tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb trail).
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/app_boot.dart`: watchdog installed right after the window stage in `run()`/`runWithEnv()`; step marks at every stage boundary and around every persisted store load in `loadBootStores`.
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart`: step marks around the post-frame restore (`restore:env` / `restore:manager` / `restore:session`) so a wedge after the first frame is equally diagnosable.
- Boot-path audit (AC2): pre-frame work is inherent to the staged await boot; network surfaces are already non-blocking or guarded (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, 180 s provider connect watchdog). No blind deferrals — moving store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.

### Test Coverage
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` (new, 9 tests): ledger ordering/in-flight/cap, threshold firing, 30 s repeat, first-frame cancel, late-frame recovery line, install idempotency — all PASS.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/` — 26/26 PASS.
- CI subset (323 files: non-golden, non-`cli_visual`, `--exclude-tags integration`): 3678 passed, 108 skipped, 2 failed — both in `providers_queue_writer_io_test.dart`, caused by `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` leaking into this runner's shell env (they pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, 10/10; CI does not set the var). Golden/`cli_visual` failures in an unfiltered local run are host-locked per the ci.yml golden comment.

### Notes
- Cannot repro on an iOS device from this environment; the build-gap statement (AC1) stands on the stale-TestFlight-build root (#1472/#1482). Next stale freeze will carry the exact boot step in Crashlytics breadcrumbs / debug logs.
- Behavior is additive-only; the watchdog never changes boot semantics.

## PR Description

## gh-1507: Boot-path main-isolate hang — boot watchdog + boot-step breadcrumbs

### Root Cause
TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch (iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) with no crash log. The freeze signature matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads) before `runApp`, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs more awaited main-isolate disk reads behind the boot spinner. With only a screenshot report and no sysdiagnose, the exact wedged step was unidentifiable — and the reporting build was 12 versions behind main because the TestFlight leg was failing (#1472, fixed in #1482).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` (new): `BootSteps` — a process-wide boot-step ledger (step name + uptime, in-flight step tracking); `BootWatchdog` — fires a diagnostic breadcrumb if the first frame does not land within the threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS=` override, `0` disables), then re-fires every 30 s until the first frame; a late first frame logs the recovery with uptime and firing count. Breadcrumbs ride the existing `debugPrint` tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb trail).
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/app_boot.dart`: watchdog installed right after the window stage in `run()`/`runWithEnv()`; step marks at every stage boundary and around every persisted store load in `loadBootStores`.
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart`: step marks around the post-frame restore (`restore:env` / `restore:manager` / `restore:session`) so a wedge after the first frame is equally diagnosable.
- Boot-path audit (AC2): pre-frame work is inherent to the staged await boot; network surfaces are already non-blocking or guarded (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, 180 s provider connect watchdog). No blind deferrals — moving store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.

### Test Coverage
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` (new, 9 tests): ledger ordering/in-flight/cap, threshold firing, 30 s repeat, first-frame cancel, late-frame recovery line, install idempotency — all PASS.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/` — 26/26 PASS.
- CI subset (323 files: non-golden, non-`cli_visual`, `--exclude-tags integration`): 3678 passed, 108 skipped, 2 failed — both in `providers_queue_writer_io_test.dart`, caused by `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` leaking into this runner's shell env (they pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, 10/10; CI does not set the var). Golden/`cli_visual` failures in an unfiltered local run are host-locked per the ci.yml golden comment.

### Notes
- Cannot repro on an iOS device from this environment; the build-gap statement (AC1) stands on the stale-TestFlight-build root (#1472/#1482). Next stale freeze will carry the exact boot step in Crashlytics breadcrumbs / debug logs.
- Behavior is additive-only; the watchdog never changes boot semantics.

## PR Description

Closes #1507
## gh-1507: Boot-path main-isolate hang — boot watchdog + boot-step breadcrumbs

### Root Cause
TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch (iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) with no crash log. The freeze signature matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads) before `runApp`, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs more awaited main-isolate disk reads behind the boot spinner. With only a screenshot report and no sysdiagnose, the exact wedged step was unidentifiable — and the reporting build was 12 versions behind main because the TestFlight leg was failing (#1472, fixed in #1482).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` (new): `BootSteps` — a process-wide boot-step ledger (step name + uptime, in-flight step tracking); `BootWatchdog` — fires a diagnostic breadcrumb if the first frame does not land within the threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS=` override, `0` disables), then re-fires every 30 s until the first frame; a late first frame logs the recovery with uptime and firing count. Breadcrumbs ride the existing `debugPrint` tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb trail).
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/app_boot.dart`: watchdog installed right after the window stage in `run()`/`runWithEnv()`; step marks at every stage boundary and around every persisted store load in `loadBootStores`.
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart`: step marks around the post-frame restore (`restore:env` / `restore:manager` / `restore:session`) so a wedge after the first frame is equally diagnosable.
- Boot-path audit (AC2): pre-frame work is inherent to the staged await boot; network surfaces are already non-blocking or guarded (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, 180 s provider connect watchdog). No blind deferrals — moving store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.

### Test Coverage
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` (new, 9 tests): ledger ordering/in-flight/cap, threshold firing, 30 s repeat, first-frame cancel, late-frame recovery line, install idempotency — all PASS.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/` — 26/26 PASS.
- CI subset (323 files: non-golden, non-`cli_visual`, `--exclude-tags integration`): 3678 passed, 108 skipped, 2 failed — both in `providers_queue_writer_io_test.dart`, caused by `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` leaking into this runner's shell env (they pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, 10/10; CI does not set the var). Golden/`cli_visual` failures in an unfiltered local run are host-locked per the ci.yml golden comment.

### Notes
- Cannot repro on an iOS device from this environment; the build-gap statement (AC1) stands on the stale-TestFlight-build root (#1472/#1482). Next stale freeze will carry the exact boot step in Crashlytics breadcrumbs / debug logs.
- Behavior is additive-only; the watchdog never changes boot semantics.

## TestFlight feedback (raw: feedback.json, no crash log attached)

- **Report**: "Just freezed" — app uptime **3000 ms** at report time (freeze ~3s after launch, i.e. during boot)
- Build: **1.0.536 (216)** — 12 versions behind main (1.0.548); the TestFlight leg has been failing (#1472), so testers run stale builds
- Device: iPhone16,1 (iPhone 15 Pro), iOS 27.0.1, arm64e, Wi-Fi, disk 3.4 GB free of 114 GB, battery 40%

Not a crash (no .ips attached) — a **hang/freeze during startup**, i.e. main-isolate block or deadlock in the boot path.

## Suspects (boot path, first ~3s)

Boot-path main-isolate work to audit for blocking IO / unawaited deadlocks:
1. Session/keys restore (`SessionKeysStore`, folder model pin restore)
2. Memory index / Obsidian vault scan at boot
3. Messaging fabric watcher + unified-root migration (`~/.fah/messages`)
4. Any synchronous network call before first frame (provider catalog fetch — the 180s connect watchdog covers provider streams, NOT app boot fetches)
5. JS/widget engine warmup, on-device model init (gemma/webllm lazy?)

## Acceptance

1. Repro attempt on current main build (1.0.548+) — cold start on iOS device, watch for boot hang; if unreproducible on current build, state which change since 1.0.536 plausibly fixed it.
2. Boot-path audit: no blocking IO on the main isolate before first frame; every boot fetch has a timeout; heavy init deferred post-frame.
3. Add a boot watchdog: if first frame takes > N sec, log a diagnostic breadcrumb (uptime, last completed boot step) so the next TestFlight feedback is actionable without guessing.

## Notes

- Raw feedback: `feedback.json` only (TestFlight screenshot feedback without sysdiagnose). Device owner = developer (istin2007@gmail.com), so a sysdiagnose / repro is obtainable on request.

- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1507` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 104
- **Additions**: +348
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T18:58:40Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T20:38:57Z

## PR Description

Closes #1507
## gh-1507: Boot-path main-isolate hang — boot watchdog + boot-step breadcrumbs

### Root Cause
TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch (iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) with no crash log. The freeze signature matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads) before `runApp`, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs more awaited main-isolate disk reads behind the boot spinner. With only a screenshot report and no sysdiagnose, the exact wedged step was unidentifiable — and the reporting build was 12 versions behind main because the TestFlight leg was failing (#1472, fixed in #1482).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` (new): `BootSteps` — a process-wide boot-step ledger (step name + uptime, in-flight step tracking); `BootWatchdog` — fires a diagnostic breadcrumb if the first frame does not land within the threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS=` override, `0` disables), then re-fires every 30 s until the first frame; a late first frame logs the recovery with uptime and firing count. Breadcrumbs ride the existing `debugPrint` tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb trail).
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/app_boot.dart`: watchdog installed right after the window stage in `run()`/`runWithEnv()`; step marks at every stage boundary and around every persisted store load in `loadBootStores`.
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart`: step marks around the post-frame restore (`restore:env` / `restore:manager` / `restore:session`) so a wedge after the first frame is equally diagnosable.
- Boot-path audit (AC2): pre-frame work is inherent to the staged await boot; network surfaces are already non-blocking or guarded (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, 180 s provider connect watchdog). No blind deferrals — moving store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.

### Test Coverage
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` (new, 9 tests): ledger ordering/in-flight/cap, threshold firing, 30 s repeat, first-frame cancel, late-frame recovery line, install idempotency — all PASS.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/` — 26/26 PASS.
- CI subset (323 files: non-golden, non-`cli_visual`, `--exclude-tags integration`): 3678 passed, 108 skipped, 2 failed — both in `providers_queue_writer_io_test.dart`, caused by `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` leaking into this runner's shell env (they pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, 10/10; CI does not set the var). Golden/`cli_visual` failures in an unfiltered local run are host-locked per the ci.yml golden comment.

### Notes
- Cannot repro on an iOS device from this environment; the build-gap statement (AC1) stands on the stale-TestFlight-build root (#1472/#1482). Next stale freeze will carry the exact boot step in Crashlytics breadcrumbs / debug logs.
- Behavior is additive-only; the watchdog never changes boot semantics.

Boot-path main-isolate work to audit for blocking IO / unawaited deadlocks:

## PR Description

## gh-1507: Boot-path main-isolate hang — boot watchdog + boot-step breadcrumbs

### Root Cause
TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch (iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) with no crash log. The freeze signature matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads) before `runApp`, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs more awaited main-isolate disk reads behind the boot spinner. With only a screenshot report and no sysdiagnose, the exact wedged step was unidentifiable — and the reporting build was 12 versions behind main because the TestFlight leg was failing (#1472, fixed in #1482).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` (new): `BootSteps` — a process-wide boot-step ledger (step name + uptime, in-flight step tracking); `BootWatchdog` — fires a diagnostic breadcrumb if the first frame does not land within the threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS=` override, `0` disables), then re-fires every 30 s until the first frame; a late first frame logs the recovery with uptime and firing count. Breadcrumbs ride the existing `debugPrint` tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb trail).
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/app_boot.dart`: watchdog installed right after the window stage in `run()`/`runWithEnv()`; step marks at every stage boundary and around every persisted store load in `loadBootStores`.
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart`: step marks around the post-frame restore (`restore:env` / `restore:manager` / `restore:session`) so a wedge after the first frame is equally diagnosable.
- Boot-path audit (AC2): pre-frame work is inherent to the staged await boot; network surfaces are already non-blocking or guarded (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, 180 s provider connect watchdog). No blind deferrals — moving store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.

### Test Coverage
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` (new, 9 tests): ledger ordering/in-flight/cap, threshold firing, 30 s repeat, first-frame cancel, late-frame recovery line, install idempotency — all PASS.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/` — 26/26 PASS.
- CI subset (323 files: non-golden, non-`cli_visual`, `--exclude-tags integration`): 3678 passed, 108 skipped, 2 failed — both in `providers_queue_writer_io_test.dart`, caused by `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` leaking into this runner's shell env (they pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, 10/10; CI does not set the var). Golden/`cli_visual` failures in an unfiltered local run are host-locked per the ci.yml golden comment.

### Notes
- Cannot repro on an iOS device from this environment; the build-gap statement (AC1) stands on the stale-TestFlight-build root (#1472/#1482). Next stale freeze will carry the exact boot step in Crashlytics breadcrumbs / debug logs.
- Behavior is additive-only; the watchdog never changes boot semantics.

The freeze signature matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads) before `runApp`, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs more awaited main-isolate disk reads behind the boot spinner. With only a screenshot report and no sysdiagnose, the exact wedged step was unidentifiable — and the reporting build was 12 versions behind main because the TestFlight leg was failing (#1472, fixed in #1482).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` (new): `BootSteps` — a process-wide boot-step ledger (step name + uptime, in-flight step tracking); `BootWatchdog` — fires a diagnostic breadcrumb if the first frame does not land within the threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS=` override, `0` disables), then re-fires every 30 s until the first frame; a late first frame logs the recovery with uptime and firing count. Breadcrumbs ride the existing `debugPrint` tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb trail).
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/app_boot.dart`: watchdog installed right after the window stage in `run()`/`runWithEnv()`; step marks at every stage boundary and around every persisted store load in `loadBootStores`.
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart`: step marks around the post-frame restore (`restore:env` / `restore:manager` / `restore:session`) so a wedge after the first frame is equally diagnosable.
- Boot-path audit (AC2): pre-frame work is inherent to the staged await boot; network surfaces are already non-blocking or guarded (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, 180 s provider connect watchdog). No blind deferrals — moving store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.

### Test Coverage
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` (new, 9 tests): ledger ordering/in-flight/cap, threshold firing, 30 s repeat, first-frame cancel, late-frame recovery line, install idempotency — all PASS.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/` — 26/26 PASS.
- CI subset (323 files: non-golden, non-`cli_visual`, `--exclude-tags integration`): 3678 passed, 108 skipped, 2 failed — both in `providers_queue_writer_io_test.dart`, caused by `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` leaking into this runner's shell env (they pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, 10/10; CI does not set the var). Golden/`cli_visual` failures in an unfiltered local run are host-locked per the ci.yml golden comment.

### Notes
- Cannot repro on an iOS device from this environment; the build-gap statement (AC1) stands on the stale-TestFlight-build root (#1472/#1482). Next stale freeze will carry the exact boot step in Crashlytics breadcrumbs / debug logs.
- Behavior is additive-only; the watchdog never changes boot semantics.

- **Author**: ai-teammate

- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 104

## PR Description

Closes #1507
## gh-1507: Boot-path main-isolate hang — boot watchdog + boot-step breadcrumbs

### Root Cause
TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch (iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) with no crash log. The freeze signature matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads) before `runApp`, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs more awaited main-isolate disk reads behind the boot spinner. With only a screenshot report and no sysdiagnose, the exact wedged step was unidentifiable — and the reporting build was 12 versions behind main because the TestFlight leg was failing (#1472, fixed in #1482).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` (new): `BootSteps` — a process-wide boot-step ledger (step name + uptime, in-flight step tracking); `BootWatchdog` — fires a diagnostic breadcrumb if the first frame does not land within the threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS=` override, `0` disables), then re-fires every 30 s until the first frame; a late first frame logs the recovery with uptime and firing count. Breadcrumbs ride the existing `debugPrint` tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb trail).
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/app_boot.dart`: watchdog installed right after the window stage in `run()`/`runWithEnv()`; step marks at every stage boundary and around every persisted store load in `loadBootStores`.
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart`: step marks around the post-frame restore (`restore:env` / `restore:manager` / `restore:session`) so a wedge after the first frame is equally diagnosable.
- Boot-path audit (AC2): pre-frame work is inherent to the staged await boot; network surfaces are already non-blocking or guarded (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, 180 s provider connect watchdog). No blind deferrals — moving store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.

### Test Coverage
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` (new, 9 tests): ledger ordering/in-flight/cap, threshold firing, 30 s repeat, first-frame cancel, late-frame recovery line, install idempotency — all PASS.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/` — 26/26 PASS.
- CI subset (323 files: non-golden, non-`cli_visual`, `--exclude-tags integration`): 3678 passed, 108 skipped, 2 failed — both in `providers_queue_writer_io_test.dart`, caused by `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` leaking into this runner's shell env (they pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, 10/10; CI does not set the var). Golden/`cli_visual` failures in an unfiltered local run are host-locked per the ci.yml golden comment.

### Notes
- Cannot repro on an iOS device from this environment; the build-gap statement (AC1) stands on the stale-TestFlight-build root (#1472/#1482). Next stale freeze will carry the exact boot step in Crashlytics breadcrumbs / debug logs.
- Behavior is additive-only; the watchdog never changes boot semantics.

## PR Description

## gh-1507: Boot-path main-isolate hang — boot watchdog + boot-step breadcrumbs

### Root Cause
TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch (iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) with no crash log. The freeze signature matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads) before `runApp`, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs more awaited main-isolate disk reads behind the boot spinner. With only a screenshot report and no sysdiagnose, the exact wedged step was unidentifiable — and the reporting build was 12 versions behind main because the TestFlight leg was failing (#1472, fixed in #1482).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` (new): `BootSteps` — a process-wide boot-step ledger (step name + uptime, in-flight step tracking); `BootWatchdog` — fires a diagnostic breadcrumb if the first frame does not land within the threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS=` override, `0` disables), then re-fires every 30 s until the first frame; a late first frame logs the recovery with uptime and firing count. Breadcrumbs ride the existing `debugPrint` tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb trail).
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/app_boot.dart`: watchdog installed right after the window stage in `run()`/`runWithEnv()`; step marks at every stage boundary and around every persisted store load in `loadBootStores`.
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart`: step marks around the post-frame restore (`restore:env` / `restore:manager` / `restore:session`) so a wedge after the first frame is equally diagnosable.
- Boot-path audit (AC2): pre-frame work is inherent to the staged await boot; network surfaces are already non-blocking or guarded (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, 180 s provider connect watchdog). No blind deferrals — moving store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.

### Test Coverage
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` (new, 9 tests): ledger ordering/in-flight/cap, threshold firing, 30 s repeat, first-frame cancel, late-frame recovery line, install idempotency — all PASS.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/` — 26/26 PASS.
- CI subset (323 files: non-golden, non-`cli_visual`, `--exclude-tags integration`): 3678 passed, 108 skipped, 2 failed — both in `providers_queue_writer_io_test.dart`, caused by `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` leaking into this runner's shell env (they pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, 10/10; CI does not set the var). Golden/`cli_visual` failures in an unfiltered local run are host-locked per the ci.yml golden comment.

### Notes
- Cannot repro on an iOS device from this environment; the build-gap statement (AC1) stands on the stale-TestFlight-build root (#1472/#1482). Next stale freeze will carry the exact boot step in Crashlytics breadcrumbs / debug logs.
- Behavior is additive-only; the watchdog never changes boot semantics.

Key considerations:

1. **Watchdog timer fires while the app might be in a wedged state**: `BootWatchdog` uses `Timer` which runs on the event loop. If the main isolate is *blocked* (synchronous CPU work), the timer won't fire — that's inherent and fine (documented behavior not mentioned, but acceptable). If it's an unawaited deadlock (awaiting never-completing futures), timer fires fine.

2. **`firstFrame()` is only called via postFrameCallback — but if the boot wedges pre-frame, the callback never fires, so repeat breadcrumbs continue every 30s. Fine.

3. **The watchdog never fires if `bootServices()` throws before routes?** Install happens after bootWindow, before bootServices. If an exception escapes, run() fails — app may not start. Timer still fires breadcrumb... `run()` errors — unhandled future error. Existing behavior. OK.

4. **`_BootstrapScreen._boot` marks**: `restore:session` completes after `createOrResumeSession` — that's post-frame restore, so the watchdog is already cancelled by first frame. These marks only serve future breadcrumb? Post-frame, watchdog is cancelled, so `restore:*` marks only matter if the frame hasn't landed... Wait, the PR description says "the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → ... ) runs more awaited main-isolate disk reads behind the boot spinner." So _BootstrapScreen builds the boot spinner, meaning a frame HAS landed (the spinner frame). So after the first frame, the watchdog cancels and the restore: marks are never consumed by the watchdog. That's a real gap: AC says "a wedge after the first frame is equally diagnosable", but with the current design, once the first frame lands the watchdog is cancelled and stops firing — a hang during restore:session would produce NO breadcrumbs. The PR description claims "step marks around the post-frame restore so a wedge after the first frame is equally diagnosable" — but the watchdog won't report post-frame wedges. ## PR Description

## gh-1507: Boot-path main-isolate hang — boot watchdog + boot-step breadcrumbs

### Root Cause
TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch (iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) with no crash log. The freeze signature matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads) before `runApp`, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs more awaited main-isolate disk reads behind the boot spinner. With only a screenshot report and no sysdiagnose, the exact wedged step was unidentifiable — and the reporting build was 12 versions behind main because the TestFlight leg was failing (#1472, fixed in #1482).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` (new): `BootSteps` — a process-wide boot-step ledger (step name + uptime, in-flight step tracking); `BootWatchdog` — fires a diagnostic breadcrumb if the first frame does not land within the threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS=` override, `0` disables), then re-fires every 30 s until the first frame; a late first frame logs the recovery with uptime and firing count. Breadcrumbs ride the existing `debugPrint` tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb trail).
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/app_boot.dart`: watchdog installed right after the window stage in `run()`/`runWithEnv()`; step marks at every stage boundary and around every persisted store load in `loadBootStores`.
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart`: step marks around the post-frame restore (`restore:env` / `restore:manager` / `restore:session`) so a wedge after the first frame is equally diagnosable.
- Boot-path audit (AC2): pre-frame work is inherent to the staged await boot; network surfaces are already non-blocking or guarded (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, 180 s provider connect watchdog). No blind deferrals — moving store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.

### Test Coverage
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` (new, 9 tests): ledger ordering/in-flight/cap, threshold firing, 30 s repeat, first-frame cancel, late-frame recovery line, install idempotency — all PASS.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/` — 26/26 PASS.
- CI subset (323 files: non-golden, non-`cli_visual`, `--exclude-tags integration`): 3678 passed, 108 skipped, 2 failed — both in `providers_queue_writer_io_test.dart`, caused by `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` leaking into this runner's shell env (they pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, 10/10; CI does not set the var). Golden/`cli_visual` failures in an unfiltered local run are host-locked per the ci.yml golden comment.

### Notes
- Cannot repro on an iOS device from this environment; the build-gap statement (AC1) stands on the stale-TestFlight-build root (#1472/#1482). Next stale freeze will carry the exact boot step in Crashlytics breadcrumbs / debug logs.
- Behavior is additive-only; the watchdog never changes boot semantics.

Key considerations:

1. **Watchdog timer fires while the app might be in a wedged state**: `BootWatchdog` uses `Timer` which runs on the event loop. If the main isolate is *blocked* (synchronous CPU work), the timer won't fire — that's inherent and fine (documented behavior not mentioned, but acceptable). If it's an unawaited deadlock (awaiting never-completing futures), timer fires fine.

2. **`firstFrame()` is only called via postFrameCallback — but if the boot wedges pre-frame, the callback never fires, so repeat breadcrumbs continue every 30s. Fine.

3. **The watchdog never fires if `bootServices()` throws before routes?** Install happens after bootWindow, before bootServices. If an exception escapes, run() fails — app may not start. Timer still fires breadcrumb... `run()` errors — unhandled future error. Existing behavior. OK.

4. **`_BootstrapScreen._boot` marks**: `restore:session` completes after `createOrResumeSession` — that's post-frame restore, so the watchdog is already cancelled by first frame. These marks only serve future breadcrumb? Post-frame, watchdog is cancelled, so `restore:*` marks only matter if the frame hasn't landed... Actually the BootstrapScreen is rendered only after first frame? Hmm — `BootstrapScreen` is presumably the widget shown by runApp (boot spinner). Wait, the PR description says "the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → ... ) runs more awaited main-isolate disk reads behind the boot spinner." So _BootstrapScreen builds the boot spinner, meaning a frame HAS landed (the spinner frame). So after the first frame, the watchdog cancels and the restore: marks are never consumed by the watchdog. That's a real gap: AC says "a wedge after the first frame is equally diagnosable", but with the current design, once the first frame lands the watchdog is cancelled and stops firing — a hang during restore:session would produce NO breadcrumbs. The PR description claims "step marks around the post-frame restore so a wedge after the first frame is equally diagnosable" — but the watchdog won't report post-frame wedges. Is there any repeat mechanism? No — firstFrame() cancels permanently. So the restore marks are recorded in the ledger but nothing ever reads them after cancellation. That's an important correctness gap vs the stated intent (AC3-ish/diagnosability of post-frame wedge). Actually the ticket AC3 only requires breadcrumb if first frame takes >N sec. - **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1507` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 104
- **Additions**: +348
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T18:58:40Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T20:38:57Z

## PR Description

Closes #1507
## gh-1507: Boot-path main-isolate hang — boot watchdog + boot-step breadcrumbs

### Root Cause
TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch (iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) with no crash log. The freeze signature matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads) before `runApp`, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs more awaited main-isolate disk reads behind the boot spinner. With only a screenshot report and no sysdiagnose, the exact wedged step was unidentifiable — and the reporting build was 12 versions behind main because the TestFlight leg was failing (#1472, fixed in #1482).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` (new): `BootSteps` — a process-wide boot-step ledger (step name + uptime, in-flight step tracking); `BootWatchdog` — fires a diagnostic breadcrumb if the first frame does not land within the threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS=` override, `0` disables), then re-fires every 30 s until the first frame; a late first frame logs the recovery with uptime and firing count. Breadcrumbs ride the existing `debugPrint` tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb trail).
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/app_boot.dart`: watchdog installed right after the window stage in `run()`/`runWithEnv()`; step marks at every stage boundary and around every persisted store load in `loadBootStores`.
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart`: step marks around the post-frame restore (`restore:env` / `restore:manager` / `restore:session`) so a wedge after the first frame is equally diagnosable.
- Boot-path audit (AC2): pre-frame work is inherent to the staged await boot; network surfaces are already non-blocking or guarded (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, 180 s provider connect watchdog). No blind deferrals — moving store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.

### Test Coverage
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` (new, 9 tests): ledger ordering/in-flight/cap, threshold firing, 30 s repeat, first-frame cancel, late-frame recovery line, install idempotency — all PASS.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/` — 26/26 PASS.
- CI subset (323 files: non-golden, non-`cli_visual`, `--exclude-tags integration`): 3678 passed, 108 skipped, 2 failed — both in `providers_queue_writer_io_test.dart`, caused by `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` leaking into this runner's shell env (they pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, 10/10; CI does not set the var). Golden/`cli_visual` failures in an unfiltered local run are host-locked per the ci.yml golden comment.

### Notes
- Cannot repro on an iOS device from this environment; the build-gap statement (AC1) stands on the stale-TestFlight-build root (#1472/#1482). Next stale freeze will carry the exact boot step in Crashlytics breadcrumbs / debug logs.
- Behavior is additive-only; the watchdog never changes boot semantics.

Key considerations:

1. **Watchdog timer fires while the app might be in a wedged state**: `BootWatchdog` uses `Timer` which runs on the event loop. If the main isolate is *blocked* (synchronous CPU work), the timer won't fire — that's inherent and fine (documented behavior not mentioned, but acceptable). If it's an unawaited deadlock (awaiting never-completing futures), timer fires fine.

2. **`firstFrame()` is only called via postFrameCallback — but if the boot wedges pre-frame, the callback never fires, so repeat breadcrumbs continue every 30s. Fine.

3. **The watchdog never fires if `bootServices()` throws before routes?** Install happens after bootWindow, before bootServices. If an exception escapes, run() fails — app may not start. Timer still fires breadcrumb... `run()` errors — unhandled future error. Existing behavior. OK.

4. **`_BootstrapScreen._boot` marks**: `restore:session` completes after `createOrResumeSession` — that's post-frame restore, so the watchdog is already cancelled by first frame. These marks only serve future breadcrumb? Post-frame, watchdog is cancelled, so `restore:*` marks only matter if the frame hasn't landed... Actually the BootstrapScreen is rendered only after first frame? Hmm — `BootstrapScreen` is presumably the widget shown by runApp (boot spinner). Wait, the PR description says "the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → ... ) runs more awaited main-isolate disk reads behind the boot spinner." So _BootstrapScreen builds the boot spinner, meaning a frame HAS landed (the spinner frame). So after the first frame, the watchdog cancels and the restore: marks are never consumed by the watchdog. That's a real gap: AC says "a wedge after the first frame is equally diagnosable", but with the current design, once the first frame lands the watchdog is cancelled and stops firing — a hang during restore:session would produce NO breadcrumbs. The PR description claims "step marks around the post-frame restore so a wedge after the first frame is equally diagnosable" — but the watchdog won't report post-frame wedges. Is there any repeat mechanism? No — firstFrame() cancels permanently. So the restore marks are recorded in the ledger but nothing ever reads them after cancellation. That's an important correctness gap vs the stated intent (AC3-ish/diagnosability of post-frame wedge). Actually the ticket AC3 only requires breadcrumb if first frame takes >N sec. The restore marks aim beyond AC. Still, the claim in the PR description is misleading; the marks are dead weight unless something reads them. I'd flag as IMPORTANT: post-frame wedge won't be breadcrumbed because the watchdog stops at first frame — consider a second watchdog phase for the post-frame restore, or drop the restore marks.

Wait — could the watchdog still help? If the restore hangs, the timer was cancelled. No further firing. So yes, the restore:* marks are never emitted. Confirmed gap.

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. ## PR Description

Closes #1507
## gh-1507: Boot-path main-isolate hang — boot watchdog + boot-step breadcrumbs

### Root Cause
TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch (iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) with no crash log. The freeze signature matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads) before `runApp`, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs more awaited main-isolate disk reads behind the boot spinner. With only a screenshot report and no sysdiagnose, the exact wedged step was unidentifiable — and the reporting build was 12 versions behind main because the TestFlight leg was failing (#1472, fixed in #1482).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` (new): `BootSteps` — a process-wide boot-step ledger (step name + uptime, in-flight step tracking); `BootWatchdog` — fires a diagnostic breadcrumb if the first frame does not land within the threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS=` override, `0` disables), then re-fires every 30 s until the first frame; a late first frame logs the recovery with uptime and firing count. Breadcrumbs ride the existing `debugPrint` tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb trail).
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/app_boot.dart`: watchdog installed right after the window stage in `run()`/`runWithEnv()`; step marks at every stage boundary and around every persisted store load in `loadBootStores`.
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart`: step marks around the post-frame restore (`restore:env` / `restore:manager` / `restore:session`) so a wedge after the first frame is equally diagnosable.
- Boot-path audit (AC2): pre-frame work is inherent to the staged await boot; network surfaces are already non-blocking or guarded (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, 180 s provider connect watchdog). No blind deferrals — moving store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.

### Test Coverage
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` (new, 9 tests): ledger ordering/in-flight/cap, threshold firing, 30 s repeat, first-frame cancel, late-frame recovery line, install idempotency — all PASS.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/` — 26/26 PASS.
- CI subset (323 files: non-golden, non-`cli_visual`, `--exclude-tags integration`): 3678 passed, 108 skipped, 2 failed — both in `providers_queue_writer_io_test.dart`, caused by `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` leaking into this runner's shell env (they pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, 10/10; CI does not set the var). Golden/`cli_visual` failures in an unfiltered local run are host-locked per the ci.yml golden comment.

### Notes
- Cannot repro on an iOS device from this environment; the build-gap statement (AC1) stands on the stale-TestFlight-build root (#1472/#1482). Next stale freeze will carry the exact boot step in Crashlytics breadcrumbs / debug logs.
- Behavior is additive-only; the watchdog never changes boot semantics.

## TestFlight feedback (raw: feedback.json, no crash log attached)

- **Report**: "Just freezed" — app uptime **3000 ms** at report time (freeze ~3s after launch, i.e. during boot)
- Build: **1.0.536 (216)** — 12 versions behind main (1.0.548); the TestFlight leg has been failing (#1472), so testers run stale builds
- Device: iPhone16,1 (iPhone 15 Pro), iOS 27.0.1, arm64e, Wi-Fi, disk 3.4 GB free of 114 GB, battery 40%

Not a crash (no .ips attached) — a **hang/freeze during startup**, i.e. main-isolate block or deadlock in the boot path.

## Suspects (boot path, first ~3s)

Boot-path main-isolate work to audit for blocking IO / unawaited deadlocks:
1. Session/keys restore (`SessionKeysStore`, folder model pin restore)
2. Memory index / Obsidian vault scan at boot
3. Messaging fabric watcher + unified-root migration (`~/.fah/messages`)
4. Any synchronous network call before first frame (provider catalog fetch — the 180s connect watchdog covers provider streams, NOT app boot fetches)
5. JS/widget engine warmup, on-device model init (gemma/webllm lazy?)

## Acceptance

1. Repro attempt on current main build (1.0.548+) — cold start on iOS device, watch for boot hang; if unreproducible on current build, state which change since 1.0.536 plausibly fixed it.
2. Boot-path audit: no blocking IO on the main isolate before first frame; every boot fetch has a timeout; heavy init deferred post-frame.
3. Add a boot watchdog: if first frame takes > N sec, log a diagnostic breadcrumb (uptime, last completed boot step) so the next TestFlight feedback is actionable without guessing.

- Raw feedback: `feedback.json` only (TestFlight screenshot feedback without sysdiagnose). Device owner = developer (istin2007@gmail.com), so a sysdiagnose / repro is obtainable on request.

Now review the code for issues.

Key considerations:

1. **Watchdog timer fires while the app might be in a wedged state**: `BootWatchdog` uses `Timer` which runs on the event loop. If the main isolate is *blocked* (synchronous CPU work), the timer won't fire — that's inherent and fine (documented behavior not mentioned, but acceptable). If it's an unawaited deadlock (awaiting never-completing futures), timer fires fine.

2. **`firstFrame()` is only called via postFrameCallback — but if the boot wedges pre-frame, the callback never fires, so repeat breadcrumbs continue every 30s. Fine.

3. **The watchdog never fires if `bootServices()` throws before routes?** Install happens after bootWindow, before bootServices. If an exception escapes, run() fails — app may not start. Timer still fires breadcrumb... `run()` errors — unhandled future error. Existing behavior. OK.

4. **`_BootstrapScreen._boot` marks**: `restore:session` completes after `createOrResumeSession` — that's post-frame restore, so the watchdog is already cancelled by first frame. These marks only serve future breadcrumb? Post-frame, watchdog is cancelled, so `restore:*` marks only matter if the frame hasn't landed... Actually the BootstrapScreen is rendered only after first frame? Hmm — `BootstrapScreen` is presumably the widget shown by runApp (boot spinner). Wait, the PR description says "the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → ... ) runs more awaited main-isolate disk reads behind the boot spinner." So _BootstrapScreen builds the boot spinner, meaning a frame HAS landed (the spinner frame). So after the first frame, the watchdog cancels and the restore: marks are never consumed by the watchdog. That's a real gap: AC says "a wedge after the first frame is equally diagnosable", but with the current design, once the first frame lands the watchdog is cancelled and stops firing — a hang during restore:session would produce NO breadcrumbs. The PR description claims "step marks around the post-frame restore so a wedge after the first frame is equally diagnosable" — but the watchdog won't report post-frame wedges. Is there any repeat mechanism? No — firstFrame() cancels permanently. So the restore marks are recorded in the ledger but nothing ever reads them after cancellation. That's an important correctness gap vs the stated intent (AC3-ish/diagnosability of post-frame wedge). Actually the ticket AC3 only requires breadcrumb if first frame takes >N sec. The restore marks aim beyond AC. Still, the claim in the PR description is misleading; the marks are dead weight unless something reads them. I'd flag as IMPORTANT: post-frame wedge won't be breadcrumbed because the watchdog stops at first frame — consider a second watchdog phase for the post-frame restore, or drop the restore marks.

Wait — could the watchdog still help? If the restore hangs, the timer was cancelled. No further firing. So yes, the restore:* marks are never emitted. Confirmed gap.

5. **`BootSteps.mark` clears `_current`**: In `loadBootStores`, pattern is begin → await load → mark. If a load throws, `_current` remains set but boot fails anyway. Fine.

6. **`BootSteps.reset()` resets a running `uptime` Stopwatch shared with the watchdog instance `_uptime`**: in production nobody calls reset. In tests, if a test resets while a watchdog timer armed... tests only. OK.

7. **Race: `install()` after `bootWindow()` but `WidgetsBinding.instance` — check bootWindow exists. In app_boot, `kBootWatchdog.install()` called after `bootWindow()`. Comment says binding exists. OK.

8. **`int.fromEnvironment` const**: `static const int _defaultThresholdMs = int.fromEnvironment(...)` — const evaluation of fromEnvironment works in Dart. OK.

9. **Threshold check `if (_defaultThresholdMs <= 0) return;` — before `_timer != null` check. Fine. But `install()` is documented idempotent; if disabled, repeated installs no-op. Fine.

10. **Missing cancellation on app lifecycle?** Watchdog repeats every 30s until first frame — if the app is backgrounded during boot, breadcrumbs keep firing while backgrounded. Minor — suggestion. Not blocking.

11. **The breadcrumb message uses `debugPrint`** — tee installed by bootWindow. OK.

12. **`firstFrame` recovery log**: logs only if firings > 0. Good.

## PR Description

Closes #1507
## gh-1507: Boot-path main-isolate hang — boot watchdog + boot-step breadcrumbs

### Root Cause
TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch (iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) with no crash log. The freeze signature matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads) before `runApp`, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs more awaited main-isolate disk reads behind the boot spinner. With only a screenshot report and no sysdiagnose, the exact wedged step was unidentifiable — and the reporting build was 12 versions behind main because the TestFlight leg was failing (#1472, fixed in #1482).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` (new): `BootSteps` — a process-wide boot-step ledger (step name + uptime, in-flight step tracking); `BootWatchdog` — fires a diagnostic breadcrumb if the first frame does not land within the threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS=` override, `0` disables), then re-fires every 30 s until the first frame; a late first frame logs the recovery with uptime and firing count. Breadcrumbs ride the existing `debugPrint` tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb trail).
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/app_boot.dart`: watchdog installed right after the window stage in `run()`/`runWithEnv()`; step marks at every stage boundary and around every persisted store load in `loadBootStores`.
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart`: step marks around the post-frame restore (`restore:env` / `restore:manager` / `restore:session`) so a wedge after the first frame is equally diagnosable.
- Boot-path audit (AC2): pre-frame work is inherent to the staged await boot; network surfaces are already non-blocking or guarded (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, 180 s provider connect watchdog). No blind deferrals — moving store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.

### Test Coverage
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` (new, 9 tests): ledger ordering/in-flight/cap, threshold firing, 30 s repeat, first-frame cancel, late-frame recovery line, install idempotency — all PASS.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/` — 26/26 PASS.
- CI subset (323 files: non-golden, non-`cli_visual`, `--exclude-tags integration`): 3678 passed, 108 skipped, 2 failed — both in `providers_queue_writer_io_test.dart`, caused by `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` leaking into this runner's shell env (they pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, 10/10; CI does not set the var). Golden/`cli_visual` failures in an unfiltered local run are host-locked per the ci.yml golden comment.

### Notes
- Cannot repro on an iOS device from this environment; the build-gap statement (AC1) stands on the stale-TestFlight-build root (#1472/#1482). Next stale freeze will carry the exact boot step in Crashlytics breadcrumbs / debug logs.
- Behavior is additive-only; the watchdog never changes boot semantics.

Key considerations:

1. **Watchdog timer fires while the app might be in a wedged state**: `BootWatchdog` uses `Timer` which runs on the event loop. If the main isolate is *blocked* (synchronous CPU work), the timer won't fire — that's inherent and fine (documented behavior not mentioned, but acceptable). If it's an unawaited deadlock (awaiting never-completing futures), timer fires fine.

2. **`firstFrame()` is only called via postFrameCallback — but if the boot wedges pre-frame, the callback never fires, so repeat breadcrumbs continue every 30s. Fine.

3. **The watchdog never fires if `bootServices()` throws before routes?** Install happens after bootWindow, before bootServices. If an exception escapes, run() fails — app may not start. Timer still fires breadcrumb... `run()` errors — unhandled future error. Existing behavior. OK.

4. **`_BootstrapScreen._boot` marks**: `restore:session` completes after `createOrResumeSession` — that's post-frame restore, so the watchdog is already cancelled by first frame. These marks only serve future breadcrumb? Post-frame, watchdog is cancelled, so `restore:*` marks only matter if the frame hasn't landed... Actually the BootstrapScreen is rendered only after first frame? Hmm — `BootstrapScreen` is presumably the widget shown by runApp (boot spinner). Wait, the PR description says "the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → ... ) runs more awaited main-isolate disk reads behind the boot spinner." So _BootstrapScreen builds the boot spinner, meaning a frame HAS landed (the spinner frame). So after the first frame, the watchdog cancels and the restore: marks are never consumed by the watchdog. That's a real gap: AC says "a wedge after the first frame is equally diagnosable", but with the current design, once the first frame lands the watchdog is cancelled and stops firing — a hang during restore:session would produce NO breadcrumbs. The PR description claims "step marks around the post-frame restore so a wedge after the first frame is equally diagnosable" — but the watchdog won't report post-frame wedges. Is there any repeat mechanism? No — firstFrame() cancels permanently. So the restore marks are recorded in the ledger but nothing ever reads them after cancellation. That's an important correctness gap vs the stated intent (AC3-ish/diagnosability of post-frame wedge). Actually the ticket AC3 only requires breadcrumb if first frame takes >N sec. The restore marks aim beyond AC. Still, the claim in the PR description is misleading; the marks are dead weight unless something reads them. I'd flag as IMPORTANT: post-frame wedge won't be breadcrumbed because the watchdog stops at first frame — consider a second watchdog phase for the post-frame restore, or drop the restore marks.

Wait — could the watchdog still help? If the restore hangs, the timer was cancelled. No further firing. So yes, the restore:* marks are never emitted. Confirmed gap.

5. **`BootSteps.mark` clears `_current`**: In `loadBootStores`, pattern is begin → await load → mark. If a load throws, `_current` remains set but boot fails anyway. Fine.

6. **`BootSteps.reset()` resets a running `uptime` Stopwatch shared with the watchdog instance `_uptime`**: in production nobody calls reset. In tests, if a test resets while a watchdog timer armed... tests only. OK.

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. ## PR Description

Closes #1507
## gh-1507: Boot-path main-isolate hang — boot watchdog + boot-step breadcrumbs

### Root Cause
TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch (iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) with no crash log. The freeze signature matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads) before `runApp`, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs more awaited main-isolate disk reads behind the boot spinner. With only a screenshot report and no sysdiagnose, the exact wedged step was unidentifiable — and the reporting build was 12 versions behind main because the TestFlight leg was failing (#1472, fixed in #1482).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` (new): `BootSteps` — a process-wide boot-step ledger (step name + uptime, in-flight step tracking); `BootWatchdog` — fires a diagnostic breadcrumb if the first frame does not land within the threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS=` override, `0` disables), then re-fires every 30 s until the first frame; a late first frame logs the recovery with uptime and firing count. Breadcrumbs ride the existing `debugPrint` tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb trail).
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/app_boot.dart`: watchdog installed right after the window stage in `run()`/`runWithEnv()`; step marks at every stage boundary and around every persisted store load in `loadBootStores`.
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart`: step marks around the post-frame restore (`restore:env` / `restore:manager` / `restore:session`) so a wedge after the first frame is equally diagnosable.
- Boot-path audit (AC2): pre-frame work is inherent to the staged await boot; network surfaces are already non-blocking or guarded (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, 180 s provider connect watchdog). No blind deferrals — moving store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.

### Test Coverage
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` (new, 9 tests): ledger ordering/in-flight/cap, threshold firing, 30 s repeat, first-frame cancel, late-frame recovery line, install idempotency — all PASS.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/` — 26/26 PASS.
- CI subset (323 files: non-golden, non-`cli_visual`, `--exclude-tags integration`): 3678 passed, 108 skipped, 2 failed — both in `providers_queue_writer_io_test.dart`, caused by `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` leaking into this runner's shell env (they pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, 10/10; CI does not set the var). Golden/`cli_visual` failures in an unfiltered local run are host-locked per the ci.yml golden comment.

### Notes
- Cannot repro on an iOS device from this environment; the build-gap statement (AC1) stands on the stale-TestFlight-build root (#1472/#1482). Next stale freeze will carry the exact boot step in Crashlytics breadcrumbs / debug logs.
- Behavior is additive-only; the watchdog never changes boot semantics.

## TestFlight feedback (raw: feedback.json, no crash log attached)

- **Report**: "Just freezed" — app uptime **3000 ms** at report time (freeze ~3s after launch, i.e. during boot)
- Build: **1.0.536 (216)** — 12 versions behind main (1.0.548); the TestFlight leg has been failing (#1472), so testers run stale builds
- Device: iPhone16,1 (iPhone 15 Pro), iOS 27.0.1, arm64e, Wi-Fi, disk 3.4 GB free of 114 GB, battery 40%

Not a crash (no .ips attached) — a **hang/freeze during startup**, i.e. main-isolate block or deadlock in the boot path.

## Suspects (boot path, first ~3s)

Boot-path main-isolate work to audit for blocking IO / unawaited deadlocks:
1. Session/keys restore (`SessionKeysStore`, folder model pin restore)
2. Memory index / Obsidian vault scan at boot
3. Messaging fabric watcher + unified-root migration (`~/.fah/messages`)
4. Any synchronous network call before first frame (provider catalog fetch — the 180s connect watchdog covers provider streams, NOT app boot fetches)
5. JS/widget engine warmup, on-device model init (gemma/webllm lazy?)

## Acceptance

1. Repro attempt on current main build (1.0.548+) — cold start on iOS device, watch for boot hang; if unreproducible on current build, state which change since 1.0.536 plausibly fixed it.
2. Boot-path audit: no blocking IO on the main isolate before first frame; every boot fetch has a timeout; heavy init deferred post-frame.
3. Add a boot watchdog: if first frame takes > N sec, log a diagnostic breadcrumb (uptime, last completed boot step) so the next TestFlight feedback is actionable without guessing.

## Notes

- Raw feedback: `feedback.json` only (TestFlight screenshot feedback without sysdiagnose). Device owner = developer (istin2007@gmail.com), so a sysdiagnose / repro is obtainable on request.

## PR Description

## gh-1507: Boot-path main-isolate hang — boot watchdog + boot-step breadcrumbs

### Root Cause
TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch (iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) with no crash log. The freeze signature matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads) before `runApp`, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs more awaited main-isolate disk reads behind the boot spinner. With only a screenshot report and no sysdiagnose, the exact wedged step was unidentifiable — and the reporting build was 12 versions behind main because the TestFlight leg was failing (#1472, fixed in #1482).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` (new): `BootSteps` — a process-wide boot-step ledger (step name + uptime, in-flight step tracking); `BootWatchdog` — fires a diagnostic breadcrumb if the first frame does not land within the threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS=` override, `0` disables), then re-fires every 30 s until the first frame; a late first frame logs the recovery with uptime and firing count. Breadcrumbs ride the existing `debugPrint` tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb trail).
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/app_boot.dart`: watchdog installed right after the window stage in `run()`/`runWithEnv()`; step marks at every stage boundary and around every persisted store load in `loadBootStores`.
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart`: step marks around the post-frame restore (`restore:env` / `restore:manager` / `restore:session`) so a wedge after the first frame is equally diagnosable.
- Boot-path audit (AC2): pre-frame work is inherent to the staged await boot; network surfaces are already non-blocking or guarded (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, 180 s provider connect watchdog). No blind deferrals — moving store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.

### Test Coverage
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` (new, 9 tests): ledger ordering/in-flight/cap, threshold firing, 30 s repeat, first-frame cancel, late-frame recovery line, install idempotency — all PASS.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/` — 26/26 PASS.
- CI subset (323 files: non-golden, non-`cli_visual`, `--exclude-tags integration`): 3678 passed, 108 skipped, 2 failed — both in `providers_queue_writer_io_test.dart`, caused by `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` leaking into this runner's shell env (they pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, 10/10; CI does not set the var). Golden/`cli_visual` failures in an unfiltered local run are host-locked per the ci.yml golden comment.

### Notes
- Cannot repro on an iOS device from this environment; the build-gap statement (AC1) stands on the stale-TestFlight-build root (#1472/#1482). Next stale freeze will carry the exact boot step in Crashlytics breadcrumbs / debug logs.
- Behavior is additive-only; the watchdog never changes boot semantics.
